findings.title: Google Meet fallback crashes when destinationCalendar is empty
findings.body: create() now does `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? []` and then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` with no optional chaining. If location is Google Meet and destinationCalendar is null, undefined, or [], mainHostDestinationCalendar is undefined and this throws TypeError before any video or calendar event is created, so the booking request fails. Previously `evt.destinationCalendar?.integration` was used, which fell back to Cal Video instead of crashing. The same check only looks at index 0, so a collective event whose first destination is not Google Calendar is forced off Meet even when a later destination is Google.

findings.title: Video booking references no longer store credentialId
findings.body: In create(), referencesToCreate now sets credentialId only for calendar results (`isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`). Video results previously kept result.credentialId. handleCancelBooking deletes the meeting only when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is set and looks that credential up; with credentialId always omitted, cancelling a new booking never calls deleteMeeting, so Zoom/Daily/Meet links stay live after cancel. updateLocation() still copies result.credentialId, so only the initial create path is broken.

findings.title: Per-host calendar create still uses only the first destination
findings.body: createAllCalendarEvents loops every destination and calls createEvent with that destination's credential, but it passes the full event whose destinationCalendar array still starts with the organizer. Office 365 (CalendarService.ts createEvent around the eventsUrl built from destinationCalendar[0]), Lark (calendarId from destinationCalendar[0]), and CalDAV (BaseCalendarService filters to destinationCalendar[0].externalId) therefore run host 2's token against host 1's calendar id. Graph/Lark return 404 or throw, and CalDAV's filter can match nothing yet still return a successful NewCalendarEventType, so a booking reference is stored for an event that was never created. Google insert does look up by credentialId, but the organizer attendee email is still destinationCalendar[0].externalId (Google CalendarService.ts around the mainHostDestinationCalendar email), so a co-host event is created with another host marked organizer:true and Google can reject the insert. The no-credentialId branch (createEvent without externalId) never matches that lookup and silently writes to the Google primary calendar instead of the configured externalId, and can do so once per credential of that integration.

findings.title: Collective co-host calendars dropped when organizer has none
findings.body: evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when both eventType.destinationCalendar and organizerUser.destinationCalendar are missing, and the collective branch then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). Optional push on null is a no-op, so every co-host destination calendar collected above is discarded. createAllCalendarEvents then takes the empty/null path and its fallback filters credentials with type === "calendar", which never matches google_calendar/office365_calendar/etc. A collective booking whose first host has no destination calendar creates no host calendar events at all, which is the case this PR is meant to fix.

findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is stored on the booking
findings.body: The booking create connects only evt.destinationCalendar[0]. Booking.destinationCalendar is a single relation, and confirm.handler, the Stripe and PayPal payment webhooks, edit location, and the booking reminder all rebuild CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar from that one row (or the organizer user row) wrapped in an array. Those paths call EventManager.create/update. Collective bookings that defer calendar creation until confirmation or payment therefore never see co-host destination calendars, so only the organizer gets a calendar event. The in-memory array built for the initial request is not recoverable later.

findings.title: Google update/delete fallback can never resolve a calendar id
findings.body: updateEvent and deleteEvent now do `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId`. When externalCalendarId is null or omitted, the find compares every calendar to that same falsy value and never matches, so selectedCalendar/calendarId is undefined. Previously this fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId. updateEvent then calls Google with calendarId undefined and the reschedule/update fails; deleteEvent falls through to "primary" and leaves the event on a non-primary calendar. CalendarManager.deleteEvent still calls deleteEvent(uid, event) without an external id, and any booking reference with a null externalCalendarId hits this path. The hangout description patch in createEvent also uses selectedCalendar with no "primary" fallback after insert used `selectedCalendar || "primary"`, so a Meet event written to primary never gets the hangout link written back.

findings.title: Cancelling remaining recurring bookings does not delete each host calendar event
findings.body: The new per-reference loop wraps the recurring allRemainingBookings branch unchanged. For every calendar reference that has a credentialId, that branch ignores the reference just fetched and instead walks every organizer calendar credential and, for each remaining instance, references.find() of the first _calendar ref only, then deleteEvent on that uid. Co-host references are never selected, so their recurring events stay on the calendar. The same first event is deleted once per outer reference times every organizer calendar credential, and the credential loaded for the current reference is unused. Non-recurring cancel correctly deletes each reference with its own credential; recurring cancel does not.

findings.title: Organization slug assignment condition was inverted
findings.body: Unrelated to destination calendars, the org create payload changed from `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug })` to `...(IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})`. Previously a slug was written when team billing was disabled, and only requestedSlug was stored when billing was enabled. Now billing-disabled instances create organizations with no slug (org URLs break), and billing-enabled instances set slug immediately as well as requestedSlug, skipping the flow that waits to assign the slug. The requestedSlug ternary next to it is behavior-preserving; the slug line dropped the negation.

findings.title: updateAllCalendarEvents calls updateEvent with a missing credential
findings.body: When a calendar reference has a credentialId that is not on the EventManager user, the code loads it from the DB, but if that lookup misses (deleted credential, or app.slug absent so the rebuild is skipped) it still pushes updateEvent(credential, ...) with credential undefined. getCalendar then throws on credential.type. That rejection fails Promise.all for every calendar reference in the batch, and the catch returns synthetic failures and no longer console.errors the message it builds, so a reschedule/location update can report total failure after partially applying. createAllCalendarEvents correctly skips a missing credential; this path does not.

findings.title: Seat-merge reschedule deletes only one old calendar event
findings.body: When newBookingId is set, updateAllCalendarEvents still does booking.references.find() for a single _calendar reference and deletes only that uid. Collective bookings now store one calendar reference per host. Merging a seated booking onto an existing slot therefore removes one host's old event and leaves the other hosts' events at the old time.

findings.title: Request-reschedule does not delete co-host calendar events
findings.body: Calendar cleanup builds credentialsMap from getUsersCredentials(user.id) keyed only by credential.type, then deleteEvent uses credentialsMap.get(bookingRef.type). Collective bookings now have one calendar reference per host, often the same type (google_calendar) but different credentialIds. The map keeps a single credential for that type, and co-host credential ids on the references are ignored, so co-host events are deleted with the requesting user's token (Google 404) and remain on the co-host calendar. handleCancelBooking was updated to load credentialId from the DB; this path was not.

findings.title: Webhook destinationCalendar shape is a breaking, inconsistent change
findings.body: CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar changed from a single DestinationCalendar | null to an array, and that object is spread into BOOKING_CREATED / BOOKING_CANCELLED / BOOKING_REJECTED webhook payloads. Consumers reading payload.destinationCalendar.externalId or .integration will break; the PR is marked non-breaking and does not version the payload. Emitters also disagree on the empty value: handleNewBooking still assigns null, while confirm, cancel, payment webhooks, and the rejected webhook e2e expectation use []. BOOKING_CREATED and BOOKING_REQUESTED tests still expect null, so clients cannot rely on one empty shape either.

findings.title: Last calendar result overwrites evt.iCalUID
findings.body: While building references, every calendar result assigns evt.iCalUID = result.iCalUID. createAllCalendarEvents now returns one result per host calendar, and each Google insert has its own iCalUID. The assignment keeps only the last host's UID on the shared event object that callers use for confirmation emails and ICS. Attendee clients can then fail to match the organizer's event. The UID is also not fed into later createEvent calls, so the host events are not correlated with each other either.

findings.title: No test covers multi-host destination calendars
findings.body: The PR checklist says no tests were added. Nothing covers createAllCalendarEvents with two destination calendars, the Google Meet empty-array crash, co-host calendars when the organizer destination is null, video reference credentialId, recurring cancel of multiple calendar references, or the webhook payload shape. The only e2e edit changes BOOKING_REJECTED destinationCalendar from null to [] and would not catch these regressions.
